doc.title: Jackie Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: Forgotten records: Al Casey, Jimmy Butler and the Fats Waller tribute
summary: Overseas fans remind him of a trio record with Al Casey and Jimmy Butler, and a Fats Waller tribute with Slam Stewart, Johnny Guarnieri and Stephane Grappelli.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: No. It will come to me before— I certainly hope so. The guitar player that was with Fats Waller. Are you familiar with him?
That’s going back. It wasn’t Al Casey or somebody?

That’s who it was — I knew you could do it. Al Casey and Butler, Jimmy Butler. They were the two of them and the drum. Anyways he was Hugh Panassie’s son, who had this little, you know, recording company like. And he wanted to record different people so they said let’s put this together. So it was his idea to put us together. He had recorded Jo Jones with the Milt Buckner Trio, you know and Illinois Jacquet and all this stuff. So

they said well let’s get this, that was his idea to put us, the three of us together. And it worked out beautifully, you know? So when I go overseas sometimes, people say, “I still have that record.” I say, “Which record?” And they’ll tell you this record and I say, “Gee whiz, I forgot all about it.”
Well it’s funny that you’re not the first person I’ve talked to that may not have the records that they played on. Now to me, I say boy I want every record I played on.

That’s true, what you’re saying. Now that record, it’s hard to get. It’s on Odyssey label. And I’ve been overseas another time with Slam Stewart, Johnny Guarnieri, Pat Flowers and we did a tribute to Fats, it was called a “Tribute to Fats Waller.” And oh we recorded a lot of wonderful tunes. And some of the stuff that was recorded on Black & Blue, and Slam did some things with Johnny, who he had worked with quite a bit long before, you know with Prez and all those other guys. And so when we recorded that I got a chance to meet Stephane Grappelli while I was there, and he decided he wanted to record with us so he recorded with us. And there’s so many wonderful things that you do sometimes, just on the spur, while being on a certain scene at a certain time, you know? And that was a wonderful experience. And from that people come and say, “Well I have a record of you” with, you know that particular instance, with Johnny Guarnieri and Slam and that one with Johnny Guarnieri and Slam and Stephane. So you never know when somebody’s going to come up with something that you did. That’s the beautiful thing about recording. Because your work can go to places that you don’t go yourself, you know? That’s the beautiful thing about it.
